An expedition led by Dr. Tarkovsky ventures into the taiga to learn about the meteorite and its impact on the land. Itching for adventure, heroes from the war privately fund their own expeditions to Siberia, hoping to find artifacts, overcome challenges, and ultimately achieve glory. Expeditions has completely different mechanisms than Scythe, though the goal was to capture some of the same feelings that Scythe evokes, with a slightly darker, more supernatural theme. Expeditions is a competitive, card-driven, engine-building game of exploration. Play cards to gain power, guile, and unique worker abilities; move your mech to mysterious locations and gain cards found among the tiles; use workers, items, meteorites, and quests to enhance your mech; and use power and guile to vanquish corruption. Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Remember the once per turn rule! The worker effects can only be triggered once per turn (no matter the source). So if you've activated the worker effect once (with or without a worker), you shouldn't be able to use it again in the same turn (with or without a worker). The passive effects on Items differ from the worker effects and can trigger multiple times (unless the passive effect reads "once per turn”). Changes on BGA BGA uses the updated Aether Mirror Card from the Gears of Corruption expansion. The updated version includes a "Refresh" instant benefit and handles point values differently. BGA uses the updated Location Tile 16 (Encampment) from the Gears of Corruption expansion. The original base game tile mistakenly showed a 5+ corruption requirement instead of the intended 8+. When creating a table you can enable the Mech/Companion draft from the Gears of Corruption expansion. Players will start with variable Guile/Power and a Gold worker which acts as a Wild worker (any color). When creating a table you can enable the Maps from the Gears of Corruption expansion. When exploring new location tiles, each map token you collect will give you a reward. community_text:
[Rating: 1/10] Truly abysmal, I can’t believe Jamey Stegmaier made this. Outrageously disappointed. The single worst board game I’ve ever played, not exaggerating

[Rating: 1/10] High player count was not play tested. As most of my games are 4+ I feel that the player count on the box is misleading. I am so disappointed I will no longer order SM games prior to release.  The game left me so upset I threw it in the bin.

[Rating: 1/10] The worst modern board game I have played. I am completely baffled that people seem to enjoy it. Awful. Insufferable.

[Rating: 1/10] It somehow feels less complex than Scythe, but harder to learn, and takes significantly longer, because your opponents' moves significantly impact your own. Every game we've played with 5 players had players place almost exactly in turn order, with the player going first winning, and the player going last losing.

[Rating: 1/10] Well, it's pretty much just Scythe, with more combos. I'll give it an extra point for not pretending to be a battling game like the original, now it's immediately obvious that this is a eurogame.

[Rating: 2/10] Too high hopes. No tension. Boring moves. It doesnt matter what you do. You start and want to stop playing after two turns, because you have already seen the whole game. Artwork is awesome.

[Rating: 2/10] Very disappointing, Played at Essen. Love Scythe world and I was expecting something more. Essentially Euro with deck manipulation but you are not doing any engine. Move gather - move play - refresh. I'd wish they had meeples instead of giant unnecessary mechs. Fiddly hex Fiddly mechs

[Rating: 2/10] I loathe this game.  Which sucks, because I like the Stonemaier games’ ethos.  This game is terrible, though.  You can do two of three of: move your mech, play a card, or get a resource from the tile you are on.  It’s the world’s most sadistic pickup and deliver.  And, to top it off, it has the thing I hate most in games-  a “refresh” phase where you basically don’t get a turn.  I would rate this a 1 if it weren’t for the art and effort.  This should fade away.  It’s awful.  Don’t buy it.

[Rating: 2/10] The rules and system are rough and not well-developed.  The structure of the rulebook is poor.  The corporate attitude of selling prototype products at high prices should be strongly criticized.  Users should not allow such companies to sell extensions.

[Rating: 2/10] random asymmetrical starting configurations that are not properly balanced. Much of the game is reacting to your planned/needed turn actions being blocked by another player with no action that can be taken to prevent this next turn. Poor iconography and lots or card text to read, compounded by the common action of resetting all the cards. The artwork on the cards is prioritized over the card use/ability within the game. [Rating: 2/10] I loved Scythe but this game sucks! Stonemaier hasn't put out a good, well play tested, game in a long time. Unfortunate because I wanted to like this. 2 points given for artwork. 2 out of 10.
